subject: Interactive latency guarantees for hosted API — cadence, carveouts, and audit hooks
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ramirez <elena@farsight.ai>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Interactive latency guarantees for hosted API — cadence & initial carveout proposal

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — great to see Farsight's conversational pipeline in action. Per our conversation you asked for concrete latency commitments for interactive calls (user-facing text generation) as part of the commercial proposal so your SREs can plan fallbacks.

Proposed SLOs (hosted API):
- P50 (interactive): 60 ms
- P95 (interactive): 300 ms

Measurement approach (high level):
- Micro-buckets: 5-minute sampling buckets across each region
- Aggregation window: rolling 60-minute sliding window composed of the micro-buckets; p50/p95 measured over the window
- Daily baseline: a rolling 24-hour median to suppress day-of-week noise for trend analysis (not applied to SLO breach calculation)

Transient relief / carveout (initial ask):
- A one-time migration carveout window request up to 8 hours during the switchover period where Farsight will onboard heavy prefix-warm traffic. Requests in that window will be tagged and excluded from SLO calculation provided Redwood routing rules for priority continuations are used.

Operational hooks we can provide immediately:
- Token-level latency traces for sampled requests via the Console link (we can grant view-only access to your SREs)
- A short audit artifact package (CSV) with micro-bucket latencies on request
- Quick mitigation: temporary dedicated routing pool (2x weight) for the first 72 hours after cutover

I've attached a measurement_recipe that explains micro-buckets and how we treat KV-cache warms and canary traffic. If this aligns, I'll pull Lauren into contracts and Priyom for the formal carveout wording and DocuSign addendum.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0193

Attachment: slo_measurement_recipe_v2.pdf (7 pages)

From: Elena Ramirez <elena@farsight.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops+contracts@farsight.ai
Date: 2027-08-06T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Interactive latency guarantees for hosted API — cadence & initial carveout proposal

Marcus —

Thanks. Overall this looks reasonable but two quick asks from our SRE/infra side: 1) we need clarity on how prefix/KV warming is detected and excluded; 2) we need a shorter carveout window (we can accept 4 hours, not 8) provided Redwood commits to the routing mitigation during that period.

Also want an explicit statement about measurement clock sync (our auditors require that both sides use NTP-verified timestamps for sample aggregation). Can you include that in the draft?

If you can send the draft carveout language + a small sample CSV showing 5-minute buckets from a prior onboarding, we can accelerate internal approval.

— Elena
Elena Ramirez
Head of Infrastructure, Farsight AI
elena@farsight.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ramirez <elena@farsight.ai>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-07T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Interactive latency guarantees for hosted API — cadence & initial carveout proposal

Elena —

Great points. Quick answers + updated commitments: 

1) Prefix / KV warming detection
- We tag requests that see >1.5x baseline KV miss rate for the client model variant within the micro-bucket; those micro-buckets are flagged and can be excluded from SLO calc if present in >50% of the bucket's calls. We record the reason code (KV_WARM or MODEL_LOAD) in the audit CSV.

2) Carveout window
- Agreed: reduce the migration carveout to a 4-hour window. During that window Redwood will: 1) enable dedicated routing pool at 2x weight, 2) prioritize your requests to the warmest hosts, 3) tag excluded micro-buckets in the audit artifact.

3) Clock sync / auditability
- Redwood will use NTP-synced timestamps for our aggregation pipeline and include the upstream request.timestamp header in the sample dump. We'll sign the DocuSign addendum with the clause that both parties attest to NTP-sync during the carveout.

Attached: a sample micro-bucket CSV (5-minute buckets, anonymized) and a one-page carveout clause draft. I'll loop in Lauren for contractual language.

Next steps I propose:
- Lauren drafts the addendum + DocuSign link
- Naomi prepares the console access for your SREs (read-only)
- Priyom reviews the carveout metric thresholds for product sign-off

If you confirm the 4-hour window we can get a DocuSign ready today.

— Marcus
Attachment: redwood_migration_carveout_summary.xlsx (sample buckets)

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ramirez <elena@farsight.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-08T14:11:00-07:00
Subject: Draft addendum language for Farsight carveout (for review)

Hi Elena / Marcus —

I've drafted a short addendum that captures:
- The p50/p95 numeric commitments (see Marcus' levels)
- Measurement methodology (5-min micro-buckets aggregated into rolling 60-min window)
- Migration carveout: single 4-hour window during onboarding; carveout applies only to micro-buckets flagged with Redwood reason codes KV_WARM or MODEL_LOAD
- Audit artifacts: Redwood will provide a CSV and two console reports within 48 hours of request

Contract snippet (for redline):
"During the single migration carveout window, Customer-identified onboarding traffic that is tagged by Redwood with reason codes KV_WARM or MODEL_LOAD will be excluded from SLO calculations. Redwood will provide audit artifacts and sample traces as described in Appendix A. The carveout window shall be scheduled with 48 hours' notice and may not exceed four (4) consecutive hours."

Priyom — can you confirm the threshold language ("flagged with reason codes... present in >50% of bucket's calls") is implementable? Naomi — please confirm console sharing steps for Farsight SREs.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

From: Elena Ramirez <elena@farsight.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops+contracts@farsight.ai
Date: 2027-08-09T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft addendum language for Farsight carveout (for review)

Lauren / Marcus —

Thanks — this is clear and we can accept the wording with one minor edit: we need the carveout to be schedulable up to 72 hours in advance (48 is OK, but we'd prefer 72) because our migration day requires operational windows across multiple teams. If Redwood accepts 72 hours' notice we will sign the addendum and execute DocuSign.

Also please include the line Marcus suggested about NTP-synced timestamps and that Redwood will include the upstream request.timestamp header in the audit CSV. Once that's included, ops+contracts will route the DocuSign to our legal.

Requesting the addendum + DocuSign link today.

— Elena
Elena Ramirez
Head of Infrastructure, Farsight AI
elena@farsight.ai
